title: Holdings view database timeouts during a rollout and a provider-status question
telemetry: Supplied Cloud Monitoring request charts and sanitized cloud_run_revision request and application logs for holdings-view, a Service Health API export made by the cloud platform owner, a TLC participant's public status-dashboard note, and owner-supplied database, neighbouring-service and release records. Each source remains separately identified; the candidate has no console, API, support-portal or database access.
owner: Thandiwe, Holdings on-call, owns the investigation; Bartholomew, the holdings-view application and release owner, owns its code, rollout and any rollback; Ingrid, the cloud platform owner, holds the project's Personalized Service Health access and the Google Cloud support relationship; the holdings-db and ledger-reports owners own their services. ITO coordinates the existing TLC and change approvals.
task: Thandiwe has asked for a bounded investigation of holdings-view HTTP 5xx responses reported from 10:12 UTC while release 7.4.0 was rolling out. TLC participants are asking whether this is a Google Cloud problem and whether to roll back. Review the supplied console observations and return an evidence-grounded technical update for the existing TLC: whether the provider-health evidence matches the observed impact, what the scope and change records support, whether recovery is established, remaining unknowns, and the next useful check with its owner. No change is authorized.

sources.claim: A Service Health event carries eventImpacts (products and locations), startTime, endTime, updateTime and updates from Google. Relevance IMPACTED means the incident is verified to impact the project; PARTIALLY_RELATED means it concerns a product the project uses but may not impact the project. State CLOSED with detailedState RESOLVED means the incident no longer affects any Google Cloud product: a provider statement, not a measurement of the customer's own user outcomes. The page does not list EventImpact subfields; the fixture's product/location rows are authored.

Personalized Service Health is the primary channel and a corroboration signal for incident response; limited-scope incidents (single location, zone or subset of projects) are communicated through PSH, while the public Cloud Service Health page carries broad severe incidents. The page gives no posting or update timing.

The public dashboard lists broad, severe incidents or serves when PSH is unavailable; an issue not listed there may be isolated to the customer's projects or a limited number of customers. Customers with a paid support plan can report an incident by creating a support case and can link a case to a known issue; in this case that is the platform owner's action.

Review an event's scope, impact and relevance to the project; projects in a different location may not be affected; if an issue does not appear to be represented in any dashboard event, contact Support. The page does not describe verifying the customer's own recovery.

The console dashboard shows incidents relevant to the project with per-product and per-location status, so partial recovery can be seen during an incident. The page does not say that the absence of an event means no issue, nor how quickly events are posted.

Cloud Run writes request, container and varlog/system logs; cloud_run_revision labels include project_id, location, service_name and revision_name. Per-revision request counts in the fixture are authored observations.

a.conclusion: A Service Health incident for Cloud SQL in us-east4, marked IMPACTED for this project, starts at 10:09, three minutes before holdings-view's 10:12 onset, and ledger-reports, which had no release, failed new Cloud SQL connections over the same interval. Release 7.4.0 served 10% at baseline before onset and changed no database settings, so a release regression is unsupported. Google closed the event as RESOLVED at 10:50 and ledger-reports returned to baseline, but holdings-view still returns 6-7% 5xx through 10:56: recovery is not established and why holdings-view lags is unknown.
next_checks: Bartholomew examines holdings-view's database connection pool and instance state after 10:50 against the 10:50-10:56 holdings-db establishment times; any recovery action, such as recycling instances, is his decision under ITO approval, and a rollback is not indicated.
Ingrid follows the event's updates and, if holdings-view impact persists, decides whether to open or link a support case to the event.

Thandiwe watches holdings-view 5xx and connection timeouts after 10:56 and reports recovery on the existing TLC only from holdings-view user outcomes, not from the provider's RESOLVED state or ledger-reports' recovery.
unsupported: Attributing the 5xx to release 7.4.0 or recommending a rollback to holdings-view-00087-mez as the fix, despite the clean 10% stage, the unchanged database settings and the matching ledger-reports impact.
Declaring holdings-view recovered because the provider event is CLOSED/RESOLVED or because ledger-reports returned to baseline.
Treating the 10:25 public-dashboard note as clearing Google Cloud for this limited-scope incident.
Presenting a failover, instance recycle, rollback or support escalation as decided or performed by the candidate.
unknowns: Why holdings-view still fails after the provider event closed and other connections recovered.
Which of the project's Cloud SQL instances the event touched; the export names project, product and location only.
holdings-view's state after the 10:56 metric coverage and 10:57 capture.

b.conclusion: Service Health shows no event for Cloud SQL or Cloud Run in us-east4; its only event is Cloud SQL in europe-west2, started before the window and marked PARTIALLY_RELATED, so it matches product but not location or time. That absence alone neither clears Google Cloud nor proves the application at fault. The local scope evidence supports a release-linked cause: 7.4.0 failed 7.0% of its 10% share while 7.3.9 stayed at 0.1%, ledger-reports on another us-east4 instance stayed at baseline, holdings-db reports baseline 0.6-0.9 s establishment, and 7.4.0 lowered the connect timeout to 0.5 s. That hypothesis is untested, and impact persists without recovery.
next_checks: Bartholomew compares 7.4.0 and 7.3.9 connection settings and timeout errors against holdings-db's establishment times; a rollback to holdings-view-00087-mez or a setting change is his decision under ITO approval.
Thandiwe tracks holdings-view 5xx and connection timeouts after 10:56 on the existing TLC; recovery is claimed only from holdings-view user outcomes.
Ingrid rechecks Service Health for us-east4 and contacts Google Cloud support only if the local checks fail to explain the timeouts.
unsupported: Attributing the impact to an unposted Google Cloud incident, or to the europe-west2 Cloud SQL event, against the per-revision, ledger-reports and holdings-db evidence.
Waiting for Google or a support case as the response while user impact persists.
Treating the absent provider event alone as proof of an application fault, or the 0.5 s setting as a confirmed cause rather than a hypothesis.
Presenting a rollback or setting change as decided or performed by the candidate, or claiming recovery.
unknowns: Whether the 7.4.0 connect-timeout change causes the failures; no comparison has been made.
Whether a narrower provider issue exists that Service Health does not represent.
holdings-view's state after the 10:56 metric coverage and 10:57 capture.
